name: Robert Frost
hook: Four Pulitzers, a snowy evening, and the roads and walls Jeopardy keeps quoting.

facts.label: the 1961 inauguration
facts.statement: Frost won four Pulitzer Prizes and in 1961 became the first poet to read at a presidential inauguration, for John F. Kennedy.

facts.label: The Road Not Taken
facts.statement: It begins 'Two roads diverged in a yellow wood' and ends 'I took the one less traveled by, / And that has made all the difference.'

facts.label: Mending Wall
facts.statement: It gives the proverb 'Good fences make good neighbors' and asks, 'Something there is that doesn't love a wall.'

facts.label: Stopping by Woods on a Snowy Evening
facts.statement: It ends 'And miles to go before I sleep,' with 'sleep' the poem's last word.
associations: miles to go before I sleep

facts.label: Fire and Ice
facts.statement: It opens 'Some say the world will end in fire, / Some say in ice.'

facts.label: The Death of the Hired Man
facts.statement: It defines home as 'the place where, when you have to go there, they have to take you in'; its last line is ''Dead,' was all he answered.'

facts.label: free verse
facts.statement: Frost said writing free verse was like 'playing tennis with the net down.'
